name: Genoa
title: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement Genoa | Hull Gauging
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Genoa for ferries, cruise ships and tankers: renewal survey gauging, pre-docking estimates and scrubber piping checks.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging in Genoa
intro: Genoa pairs a busy ship-repair district with year-round ferry, cruise and tanker traffic, so many superintendents meet a drydock or renewal survey here. When a ro-pax ferry is booked into a Genoa drydock, or a tanker at Multedo needs gauging ahead of a CAP or vetting inspection, Atlantis NDT mobilises an ultrasonic thickness measurement team from India to work to the yard programme and the attending surveyor's requirements.

highlights.h: Ferry refit season in the drydocks
highlights.p: Ro-pax operators on the Sardinia, Corsica and Sicily routes tend to dock in the quieter winter months, so renewal and intermediate survey gauging in Genoa clusters into a season that can be planned well ahead.

Crude and product tankers at the Multedo oil port can have accessible ballast tanks, deck plating and deck piping gauged during discharge, giving owners data before a CAP, a vetting inspection or a sale.

Cruise ships and ferries that return to Genoa on fixed rotations give repeat access to exhaust gas cleaning wash-water and overboard piping, so wall loss can be trended across several calls instead of measured once.

port.h: The port of Genoa and the ships that call there
p: Genoa is the principal port of the Western Ligurian Sea port system, which also takes in Savona and Vado Ligure. Its basins run along the coast from the old port westwards to Voltri-Prà, and the traffic mix is unusually broad for a single city: container ships at the Prà terminal, ro-ro and multipurpose ships in the Sampierdarena basins, overnight ferries to Sardinia, Corsica, Sicily and North Africa, cruise ships at the passenger terminals, and crude and product tankers at the Multedo oil port to the west.

For thickness gauging, the decisive feature is the ship-repair district in the eastern part of the port. Drydocks owned by the port authority and operated by Ente Bacini sit alongside repair and conversion yards with their own quays, and Genoa has long experience of ferry, cruise and conversion work. Ferry operators favour the winter months for dockings, when island timetables thin out, which concentrates renewal and intermediate survey work into a predictable season. Cruise lines that homeport ships in Genoa also use the repair berths for technical stops and refits, and these stays give time to open tanks and voids that are never accessible in service.

Inspection demand in Genoa is shaped by the ro-pax fleet. Many ferries on the Tyrrhenian routes are older tonnage, and their vehicle decks, internal ramps, stern doors, void spaces and ballast tanks accumulate wastage that each renewal survey examines more closely. Tankers at Multedo bring a different kind of request: gauging that supports CAP, vetting or a sale and has to be finished inside a discharge window. Container ships at Prà, by contrast, usually offer only short, limited-scope access during cargo work, so jobs there are planned around a defined list of spaces rather than a full survey. Ferry thickness gauging in Genoa is therefore often a two-stage job: a pre-docking survey alongside to size the steel work, then a full programme once the ship is on the blocks.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in and around Genoa
p: Most structured gauging in Genoa takes place in the ship-repair district east of the old port. In a graving or floating dock the bottom shell, side shell, sea chests and stern area are fully accessible, while repair quays let tanks be opened, ventilated and gauged with the ship afloat. Large refits and conversions involve steel renewal planning, so a pre-docking thickness survey is often done weeks earlier, sometimes at the ship's normal Genoa berth between sailings, to give the yard tonnage estimates before the contract is fixed. Ship inspection in Genoa also benefits from short distances: drydocks, repair quays and passenger terminals sit within one harbour, so a team can move between a docked ship and an afloat one in the same day.

UTM in Genoa outside the repair district is usually shorter and more targeted: a tanker at Multedo during discharge, a container ship at Prà during cargo operations, or a ship lying at the outer anchorage awaiting a berth or a sale inspection. Savona and Vado Ligure, within the same port system, add cruise and container calls that the same mobilisation can cover. Every terminal has its own ISPS access procedure, and the ship's agent handles passes and launch bookings.

Repair and conversion yards in the ship-repair district — gauging ahead of steel renewal on ferries, cruise ships and conversion projects, plus re-gauging of renewed areas
Ferry and cruise passenger terminals — afloat gauging of vehicle decks, ramps, voids and scrubber piping between overnight sailings or during turnaround days

Savona and Vado Ligure — cruise and container calls within the same port system, covered by the same mobilisation when schedules overlap

context.h: Regulatory and market context for ships calling at Genoa
p: Italy is a Paris MoU state, so ships in Genoa are selected for port state control under the Paris MoU risk-based targeting system, and visible structural wastage on an older ship can turn a routine inspection into a detention. Since 1 May 2025 the Mediterranean Sea has been a SOx Emission Control Area under MARPOL Annex VI regulation 14, so ships calling at Genoa burn 0.10% sulphur fuel or operate an exhaust gas cleaning system to an equivalent standard. Ferries and cruise ships with scrubbers now run them to ECA limits throughout Mediterranean waters, which makes wash-water piping, overboard discharge lines and their shell penetrations a regular gauging item.

EU ETS has covered shipping since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime has applied since 2025, and both bear on older ferries and tankers: when an owner weighs keeping, selling or re-engining a ship, a recent gauging record tells the buyer or the yard what steel work lies ahead. Genoa is also a centre of the Italian shipping community. RINA, the Italian classification society, has its headquarters here, as do major ferry and cruise operators, and the city hosts shipowners, managers, brokers and P&I correspondents. Superintendents planning a Genoa docking therefore often have the class, the yard and the commercial decision-makers within the same city.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Genoa
jobs.p: Most Genoa enquiries come from ferry and cruise operators planning a docking, from tanker managers who need data before CAP or vetting, and from buyers inspecting ships that are trading in or out of the Mediterranean. The common thread is a fixed window: a yard slot booked months ahead or a discharge that lasts a day. We agree the scope, the spaces and the attending surveyor's expectations before the team travels.
list: Renewal survey gauging on a ro-pax ferry in an Ente Bacini drydock, covering vehicle decks, ramps, bottom shell and ballast tanks, with results feeding the yard's steel renewal list
Pre-docking gauging on a ferry at its regular Genoa berth between overnight sailings, so the owner can fix steel tonnage with the repair yard before the docking date
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping wall-thickness survey on a homeported cruise ship during a turnaround day at the passenger terminal
Gauging of ballast tanks and main deck on a product tanker at Multedo during discharge, to close out substantial corrosion items before a CAP inspection
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a multipurpose ship at the outer anchorage, reached by launch and limited to safely accessible spaces

logistics: Genoa Cristoforo Colombo Airport sits beside the port, and longer-haul arrivals connect through Milan Malpensa or Rome Fiumicino. The ship's agent arranges ISPS gate passes for the drydocks, repair quays and terminals, or a launch for ships at anchor. Italy is in the Schengen area, so our technicians travel on Schengen visas, and we start the application as soon as a docking date is firm. That suits Genoa well: ferry and cruise dockings are normally booked months in advance, which leaves ample time to align visas, flights and the yard programme.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ferry in a Genoa drydock during its winter refit?
faqs.a: Yes. Winter dockings are the most common Genoa job. Send us the docking dates, the class survey due and the previous thickness report, and we plan the team's arrival for when tanks are open and staging is in place. Bottom shell and sea chests are best gauged in the first days, before blasting and painting crews take over.

faqs.q: Can tanker gauging at Multedo be done without gas-freeing cargo tanks?
faqs.a: Partly. During discharge we can gauge the main deck, deck piping and any ballast tanks the ship's officers declare safe for entry under the ship's permit system. Cargo tank internals need a gas-free certificate, so full CAP-level gauging of cargo tanks is normally planned for a yard stay rather than a terminal call.

faqs.q: Do you need class approval to measure on a RINA-classed ship in Genoa?
faqs.a: Under IACS UR Z17, thickness measurement credited to a class survey has to be carried out by a firm that the ship's own class society has approved, whichever society that is. Check the approval position for your ship's class with us at the scoping stage. Gauging for owners' own purposes, such as pre-docking estimates or pre-purchase inspection, is not tied to a class survey.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we book thickness measurement in Genoa?
faqs.a: As early as the docking or inspection date is known. Our team is mobilised from India and needs Schengen visas, so a few weeks of notice is the practical minimum, and more is better in the winter refit season, when yard schedules move and several ferries may be in the drydocks at once.
